review_candidates.title: Senior Program Officer, Wu’n Sina Sinru Project Lead [BENINESE NATIONALS ONLY]
review_candidates.description: About CIVIC Center for Civilians in Conflict (CIVIC) is an international nonprofit with offices around the world working to improve protection for civilians caught in conflict zones. CIVIC envisions a world in which no civilian is harmed in conflict. Our mission is to support communities affected by conflict in their quest for protection and strengthen the resolve and capacity of armed actors to prevent and respond to civilian harm. We are advocates who believe that no civilian caught in conflict should be ignored, and advisors who provide practical solutions to prevent and respond to civilian harm. Learn more at civiliansinconflict.org. About The Position The Senior Program Officer (Wu’n Sina Sinru Project Lead) will provide technical, operational, and financial leadership for the Wu’n Sina Sinru project, an action funded by the European Union and implemented by CIVIC as lead applicant, with its co-applicants Catholic Relief Services (CRS) and DEDRAS. The project aims to reduce violence and harm to civilians in four border communes of northern Benin (Ségbana, Kalalé, Nikki, and Pèrèrè, in the Alibori and Borgou departments) by strengthening the capacity of the defence and security forces (FDS) to prevent, mitigate, and respond to civilian harm; helping community protection mechanisms obtain responses from authorities and security forces; and meeting the protection needs of displaced people and host communities. The role combines project management, technical leadership on civilian harm mitigation, consortium coordination, budget oversight, and stakeholder engagement. City, Country: Parakou, Benin Duration: 12 months (renewable) Travel required: 20% required Contract Duration: 12 months Reports to: Country Director (Togo & Benin) Contract type: Fixed Work modality: On-site Key Responsibilities Technical Leadership and Program Quality Lead the technical delivery of CIVIC’s components of the Wu’n Sina Sinru project (specific objective 1 and outputs 2.1 and 2.2), ensuring quality, conflict sensitivity, and adherence to Do No Harm principles. Oversee the design, contextualization, and delivery of trainings on civilian harm mitigation (CHM) and community engagement for security and defence forces pre- and awareness sessions for local initiative security and community self-protection measures. Lead technical workshops with the Beninese armed forces and the high command on civilian harm mitigation and protection of civilians. Ensure the integration of the community protection approach into civil-military committees and civil-security dialogues, and the quality of the protection risk analyses conducted with community peace and security spaces. Lead the conflict sensitivity and protection risk analysis during the start-up phase, and ensure it is updated before each activity bringing together civilians and security actors. Project Delivery and Consortium Coordination Lead day-to-day implementation of the Wu’n Sina Sinru project in line with the work plan, the EU grant agreement, and CIVIC’s country strategy. Lead the project start-up: sub-agreements with CRS and DEDRAS, internal kick-off and launch workshop, consultations with national and communal stakeholders, and set-up of the steering committee (CIVIC, CRS, DEDRAS, ABeGIEF, ABPC, EMG-FAB, ACM cell, mayors, and the EU Delegation in Benin). Coordinate the consortium through regular technical coordination meetings, joint monitoring missions, and quarterly review cycles, ensuring coherence across the three specific objectives. Supervise the four community liaison officers based in Ségbana, Kalalé, Nikki, and Pèrèrè, and work closely with the Military Engagement Officer, the Community Engagement Officer, the Advocacy Officer, the Admin and Finance Officer, the MEAL Officer, and the leads of CIVIC’s other projects implemented in northern Benin. Ensure coordination with the cross-border action implemented in Nigeria by DRC, Search for Common Ground, and CIVIC (Bagudo, Borgu, and Baruten LGAs), including a common timeline and joint cross-border activities. Ensure the safe conduct of field activities in coordination with the security focal point. Budget Management and Financial Oversight Collaborate with the Country Director, the Country Finance, HR & Admin Manager, and the Admin and Finance Officer to plan, monitor, and forecast the Wu’n Sina Sinru budget, including partners’ sub-grants. Oversee the Local Initiatives Fund (FIL): selection of community initiatives, disbursement by tranches against agreed milestones and supporting documents, or direct payment where needed, in compliance with EU rules on financial support to third parties. Ensure responsible use of funds and compliance with the EU grant contract, CIVIC internal policies, and procurement procedures. Track budget performance and provide regular updates, forecasts, and variance analyses; contribute to interim and final financial reports to the EU. Ensure cost-effectiveness and accountability across all operational and programmatic expenditures. Capacity Building and Institutional Strengthening Mentor and build the capacity of CIVIC staff, community liaison officers, and partners (CRS, DEDRAS) in civilian protection, civilian harm mitigation, and community-based protection. Support Beninese institutions (EMG-FAB, ACM cell, ABeGIEF, ABPC) to integrate protection of civilians into their practices, training, and coordination mechanisms, including the replication of trainings by trained commanders. Support community peace and security spaces, including women, youth, and displaced people, to conduct protection analyses and carry advocacy messages to authorities and security forces. Business Development and Fundraising Identify opportunities to consolidate and scale up Wu’n Sina Sinru results in northern Benin, in coordination with the Country Director and global programs team. Contribute to concept notes, full proposals, and engagement with donor representatives, including for follow-on funding. Provide technical inputs to logframes, theories of change, and narratives for protection-related opportunities. Stakeholder Engagement and Policy Influence Represent CIVIC and the consortium with local authorities (mayors, prefects), FDS commands, ABeGIEF, ABPC, and humanitarian actors in northern Benin (UNHCR, UNICEF, WFP, ICRC, and the protection working group). Support ABeGIEF in organizing cross-border workshops on the protection of civilians in the Boo, Baatonou, and Fulani linguistic areas, and lead roadmap follow-up and advocacy meetings in Ségbana, Kalalé, Nikki, Pèrèrè, Kandi, Parakou, and Cotonou. Lead advocacy and follow-up sessions with general staffs, the Ministry of Defence, and the Operation Mirador command to translate commitments into concrete adjustments of practices. Maintain regular communication with the EU Delegation and implement the project’s visibility strategy in line with EU guidelines and Do No Harm principles. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning With the MEAL team, oversee the consortium’s joint MEAL system: common monitoring plan, baseline study, internal mid-term review at month 9, and final external evaluation. Ensure data are disaggregated by sex, age, and disability, that post-training evaluations take place three to four months after trainings, and that the register of dialogue commitments and the feedback and complaints mechanism are kept up to date. Lead the preparation of narrative reports to the EU and produce case studies, success stories, and lessons learned, in line with data protection rules. Required Qualifications Education Advanced degree in International Relations, Human Rights, Peacebuilding, Public Administration, or a closely related field, with specialized knowledge in civilian protection and conflict transformation. Experience Over 10 years of progressive experience managing civilian protection, humanitarian, or stabilization projects, including 3 years of field-based leadership in fragile and conflict-affected environments. Recognized technical expertise in the protection of civilians (PoC) and civilian harm mitigation, including engagement with security sector actors and community-based protection mechanisms. Proven experience managing projects funded by the European Union or other institutional donors, ensuring donor compliance, budget integrity, and accountability. Experience coordinating consortia or implementing partners and supervising field teams. Technical Skills Exceptional leadership, coordination, and capacity-strengthening skills. Fluency in French; proficiency in English is a strong asset; knowledge of Baatonou, Boo, or Fulfulde is an asset. Proficient in MS Office (especially Excel), project management tools (Asana/MS Project/Monday.com), and common M&E/data platforms (KoboToolbox, DHIS2). Other Requirements Eligibility to work in Benin without sponsorship Ability to travel up to 20% of the time Preferred Qualifications Familiarity with security and community dynamics in northern Benin and the Benin–Nigeria border area. Experience engaging with armed actors in sensitive political environments. Strong understanding of humanitarian architecture and donor landscape (e.g., EU, Switzerland, Netherlands, UN). Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver under pressure. Core Competencies High level of accuracy, rigor, and attention to detail Strong integrity, discretion, and sense of accountability Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines in complex environments Strong analytical and problem-solving skills Collaborative mindset and strong interpersonal skills Commitment to CIVIC's values and the Protection of Civilians Compensation Gross salary of USD 4,525 – USD 4,625 per month dependant on experience and qualifications. CIVIC typically offers a hybrid work model with work from home 2–3 days per week (depending on the location and agreement with supervisor), as well as a competitive compensation and benefits package for full time staff including health coverage, professional counseling services, a retirement savings contribution, telephone allowance, and days of paid leave plus paid holidays (including the days between Christmas and New Year's Day). review_candidates.title: Senior Manager - ASEAN-UK Sage Phase 2
review_candidates.description: Location: Jakarta, Indonesia Vacancy type: Full-time; two year fixed-term contract Service areas: Governance & Stability team About ASI ASI (Adam Smith International) is a global advisory company that works locally to transform lives by making economies stronger, societies safer, and governments more effective. We work on behalf of governments, foundations and companies that share our ambition to take on the big challenges facing the world. We develop strategies and design, deliver and evaluate programmes that stimulate economic growth, stability and good governance. For nearly three decades in almost 100 countries, we have been working in partnership with governments, the private sector and civil society in countries at all stages of development. Our core team of staff and technical experts, in multiple offices around the world, ensures the quality of delivery and high ethical standards that we and our clients require. We bring together a global network of specialist experts, who contribute their experience and know-how, where and when it is needed. This is an exciting time to join Adam Smith International and become part of a team of bright, dynamic and committed people, determined to transform lives for the better. About The Team ASI’s Governance and Stability Practice supports the design and delivery of work focused on strengthening governance and enhancing stability around the world. The practice covers education, centre of government reform, local government reform, public financial management, anti-corruption, civil society development, alongside stabilisation, security sector reform, conflict reduction and humanitarian work. The team manages a growing portfolio of programmes for the UK and other donors. We are recruiting a Senior Manager to support the delivery of the ASEAN-UK Sage Phase 2 programme and to contribute to ASI’s wider growth in Southeast Asia. The ASEAN-UK Sage Phase 2 Programme ASEAN-UK Sage Phase 2 (Sage-2) is a UK FCDO-funded programme delivered through the UK Mission to ASEAN. The programme runs from 2026-2029, with a focus on primary education - improving foundational learning across the region. The programme will provide technical assistance to countries to improve foundational learning. It aims to support ASEAN Member States to adopt, adapt and begin to institutionalise evidence-based approaches to improve foundational learning, informed by data, diagnostics and global and regional evidence. Priority countries: Cambodia, Lao PDR and Timor-Leste, with additional selective engagement in the Philippines. Core delivery areas: country level foundational learning reform support, evidence translation, learning and implementation insights, and strategic partnerships and regional engagement. About The Role We are looking to recruit a Senior Manager, based in Jakarta, to play a central role in the effective delivery of Sage-2. The role will primarily focus on programme management, client and partner engagement, delivery coordination, financial oversight, risk management and quality assurance. The role will also include a secondary focus on supporting ASI’s business growth in Southeast Asia, particularly by identifying and developing opportunities linked to education, governance, public sector reform and human development. The Senior Manager will work closely with the Project Director, Team Lead, technical leads, consortium partners, project manager, operations and finance resources, and the wider ASI team to ensure the programme is delivered to a high standard, meets FCDO requirements, contributes to sustainable reform in priority countries, and strengthens ASI’s profile in the region. Key Responsibilities Programme Delivery and Management As part of Sage-2’s leadership team, support the Project Director and Team Lead to effectively manage the delivery of the programme, ensuring plans are delivered on time, and outputs are high quality. Coordinate workplans, budgets, forecasts, delivery trackers, risk registers and reporting products. Lead the Sage-2 Project Management Unit, including line managing the Sage-2 Project Manager and Operations Manager. Support mobilisation and management of technical experts, consortium partners and downstream delivery arrangements. Track progress against agreed outputs, milestones, KPIs and deliverables. Help maintain a lean and efficient delivery model that ensures Value for Money (VfM) while enabling high-quality technical assistance. Client, partner and stakeholder engagement Support regular operational engagement with FCDO and the UK Mission to ASEAN. Prepare for and follow up on programme governance meetings, including action tracking and partner coordination. Lead communication and coordination with consortium partners and country teams on programme management matters. Support engagement with ASEAN institutions and regional education platforms where this contributes to programme objectives. Identify, escalate and help resolve delivery issues in a timely and transparent way. Technical assistance coordination and quality assurance Work with technical leads and country teams to ensure technical assistance is well planned, properly resourced and delivered to agreed standards. Support the development of annual country level workplans, reform design processes and delivery plans. Quality assure technical outputs before submission to FCDO or external stakeholders. Help ensure country-level support remains focused on institutionalisation, scale, government ownership and improved foundational learning outcomes. Learning, reporting and adaptive management Support the Learning & Adaptation Lead to capture delivery learning and apply it to programme management and adaptation. Contribute to monthly, quarterly and annual reporting, ensuring reports are accurate, concise, evidence-based and action-oriented. Ensure evidence and learning products are linked to practical decisions, programme improvement and stakeholder engagement. Financial management, risk and compliance Overall responsibility for accurate budget forecasting, expenditure tracking and invoice preparation. Monitor spend against forecast and work with finance colleagues to explain variances. Oversight of quarterly financial reporting and alignment between costed workplans, outputs and deliverables. Maintain and update programme risk registers, delivery chain information and escalation logs. Support compliance with safeguarding, duty of care, fraud, data protection, confidentiality, equality and inclusion, transparency, branding and communications requirements, in line with ASI and FCDO policies. Ensure delivery decisions are informed by VfM, including economy, efficiency, effectiveness and equity. Business Growth Identify and track relevant business development opportunities, including in Southeast Asia, particularly in education, governance, public sector reform and human development. Support ASI’s market positioning in Indonesia, ASEAN and priority countries linked to Sage Phase 2. Build and maintain networks with donors, development partners and potential consortium partners. Contribute to planning, partner identification, bid strategy and proposal development. Write or review bid sections where ASI’s programme delivery, regional engagement or education systems reform experience is relevant. , What We’re Looking For This role requires a high level of responsibility and would suit someone in their mid-career with strong programme delivery experience, sound judgement, excellent organisational skills and the ability to work confidently with senior stakeholders. Essential Experience And Skills At least seven years of relevant experience in international development, public sector reform, education systems, governance, programme management or a related field. Strong experience managing complex donor-funded programmes, ideally including FCDO-funded commercial contracts. Excellent project management skills, including workplanning, delivery tracking, budget management, forecasting, reporting, risk management and quality assurance. Strong stakeholder management skills, with experience working with donors, government counterparts, consortium partners or multilateral institutions. Experience managing or coordinating technical assistance programmes in politically or institutionally complex environments. Excellent written English, including the ability to produce clear reports, briefing notes, donor correspondence and proposal material. Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across cultures, organisations and time zones. Strong organisational skills, attention to detail and ability to manage competing priorities. Willingness to be based in Jakarta and travel regionally as required. Desirable Experience And Skills Experience working in Southeast Asia, particularly Sage-2 target countries. Experience working with ASEAN institutions, regional education platforms or regional cooperation mechanisms. Knowledge of foundational learning, basic education reform, evidence-based education programming, structured pedagogy, targeted instruction or Teaching at the Right Level. Experience supporting business development, proposal writing, market positioning or donor engagement. Experience managing consortium or downstream partner arrangements. Familiarity with MEL, adaptive management, political economy analysis, VfM and safeguarding requirements. What We Offer You Our people are at the heart of our strategy and our decisions. We offer a competitive salary and benefits package, a dynamic and friendly team environment, the opportunity to support a high-profile regional programme, and support to develop your skills and progress in your career. This is an exciting role for someone who wants to combine hands-on programme delivery with business growth. The successful candidate will help deliver a flagship ASEAN-UK education programme, support government-led reform in priority countries, and contribute to ASI’s wider growth in Southeast Asia. What Makes ASI a Great Place To Work At Impactful work: Lead and innovate in high impact portfolio of programmes that drive reach change. Grow with ASI: We offer dedicated support to develop your skills and progress in your career. Team That Inspires: Collaborate with brilliant, passionate colleagues in a dynamic environment. Diverse Workforce: Through our Equality Action Plan, our Diversity and Inclusion Committee, and through leadership from our Executive Team and oversight by our Board, we ensure ASI is a place where you can be yourself and succeed. Flexibility That Works for You: We recognise the importance of your life outside of work and support flexible working. ASI is committed to ensuring that everyone in the organisation is treated with dignity, respect, and fairness. The Company values diversity and inclusion and strives to maintain a workplace where all individuals are treated equally. ASI is committed to ensuring the safety and wellbeing of everyone involved in its work. All ASI People are responsible for understanding and following the Safeguarding Policy, which is designed to protect individuals — especially vulnerable groups — from exploitation, abuse, harassment, or violence of any kind, including sexual misconduct We'd love to hear from you Excited to join us? Submit your CV (no more than two pages) and a one-page cover letter setting out your motivations and suitability. The deadline for applications is 30/11/2026 . Due to the high volume of applications, only shortlisted applicants will be contacted. ASI encourages applications from candidates of all social backgrounds, ethnicities, genders, abilities, and orientations.
